items.title: Joel Dorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2007
items.q: through a friend, Bernie Dreighton, I found some tapes he had made at a small club in Brooklyn in the sixties

ctx.x: Yeah. No. I got a stash of tapes that no one’s ever heard. I have a way that I do compilations. I have this little area, I started playing it because when I came back after that slump in the early eighties I had to come up with something new. Because the pop records I was making and the jazz records I was making, nobody really wanted. So, this

is too long a story to bore you with but through a friend, Bernie Dreighton, I found some tapes he had made at a small club in Brooklyn in the sixties: Blakey, Kenny Dorham, you know, people like that, guys who’d play these small clubs in Brooklyn to work out material before they recorded for Blue Note or Prestige or stuff like that. So in trying to clear those, I came across other collections. At a certain point we had isolated a quarter of a million hours of privately — in lieu of the word illegally — recorded…
I noticed that when I was listening to the Cannonball thing you sent, “Radio Nights.” I’m listening to him and I’ve not heard that kind of playing on even his best records. It was somehow—
